title:
Whistles call and answer.
 
 THE CALLS Wait, my love, and I’ll be with you.
 
 
 THE ANSWERS Round behind the stable.
html_source: This exchange is mindful of the Sirens episode when Richie Goulding “cocked his lips apout,” and issued a “low incipient note sweet banshee murmured.” The whistle call of “Wait my love…” here in Circe echoes the word “wait” that appears in its sundry forms no less than fifty-five times in Sirens. The theme of waiting for love, subordinate to the greater theme in Ulysses of The Pain of Love, is brought center stage here in Circe’s stage-play setting when we recall the Siren episode’s narrator saying, “Time makes the tune.” It certainly makes the tune heard in THE CALLS' whistle here in Circe. Molly has only to wait through three more episodes (some four hours) and then Bloom “will be with [her]. In Sirens, "How sweet the answer.” How sweet THE ANSWERS of assent here in Circe.
